message.content:
{
  "decision": "APPLY",
  "workflow_yaml": "name: Publish Package 📦 to  PyPI
on:
  release:
    types: [published] # with prerelease and release

permissions:
  contents: read
  id-token: write  # IMPORTANT: this permission is mandatory for trusted publishing
jobs:
  build_and_publish:
    # Set up the environment `CI` references the secret `PYPI_API_TOKEN` in repository settings
    # https://docs.github.com/en/actions/deployment/targeting-different-environments/using-environments-for-deployment#referencing-an-environment
    environment: CI
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v2
    - name: Cache pip dependencies
      uses: actions/cache@v4
      with:
        path: ~/.cache/pip
        key: ${{ runner.os }}-pip-${{ hashFiles('pyproject.toml') }}
        restore-keys: |
          ${{ runner.os }}-pip-
    - name: Installing build Dependencies
      run: |
        python -m pip install --upgrade pip
        pip install build
    - name: Build package
      run: python -m build
    - name: Publish package
      uses: pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish@release/v1
",
  "rationale": "The P-LIT-GHA-CACHE pattern applies: this publish workflow repeatedly fetches pip dependencies (pip and the build package) on every release run, there is no existing dependency cache, and pyproject.toml provides a stable cache-input key. Adding actions/cache@v4 for ~/.cache/pip before dependency installation preserves all existing build/publish steps, permissions, and required checks while reducing repeated dependency fetch time on warm runs.",
  "evidence_ids": ["pattern:P-LIT-GHA-CACHE", "experiment:batch-hiruni-pattern-bat-ae496965ffa682a2-r2"]
}
